title: Multi-Step Problems with Strip Diagrams and Equations
seo_title: Grade 4 Multi-Step Problems with Strip Diagrams and Equations (TEKS 4.5A, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.5A represent multi-step problems involving the four operations with whole numbers using strip diagrams and equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.5A: multi-step problems with strip diagrams, equations with a letter for the unknown, times as many and two-step word problems. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Draw a strip diagram, then write an equation with a letter for the unknown.
key_sub: t = (4 × 25) + 18 shows both steps. Solve one step at a time.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A strip diagram shows how the numbers in a problem fit together: equal parts for multiplication and division, parts and a whole for addition and subtraction.
  • Write an equation with a letter for the unknown: t = (4 × 25) + 18.
  • Solve one step at a time. Use the order the story describes, and check that the answer makes sense.

Examples

Example

Ana buys 4 packs of 25 stickers and gets 18 more. How many stickers?

t = (4 × 25) + 18

4 × 25 = 100

100 + 18 = 118

Answer: 118 stickers

Example

Solve (3 × n) + 12 = 57.

57 − 12 = 45

45 ÷ 3 = 15

Answer: n = 15

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the wrong operation in step 2Ask what the story does next: adds, takes away, shares or groups.
Putting the unknown in the wrong placeThe letter stands for the number the question asks for.
Stopping after one stepReread the question: does your number answer it?

faq.a: Represent multi-step problems involving the four operations with whole numbers using strip diagrams and equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.

faq.q: Why use a letter in an equation?
faq.a: The letter stands for the unknown number, so the equation shows the whole problem before you solve it.
They show which amounts are equal parts, which are wholes and which is unknown, so you can choose the operations.

faq.q: How do I check a multi-step answer?
faq.a: Put your answer back into the story or the equation, or estimate to see if it is reasonable.

sets.title: Times as many: statements and equations

items.q: Which equation matches the bar model?
items.e: Josiah's bar is 7 equal parts, and each part is the same as Marcus's bar (8). So Josiah has 7 times as many: 7 × 8 = 56. The equation is 56 = 7 × 8.

items.q: What does the bar model show?
c: Isaac has 7 times as many as Emma
Isaac has 28 times as many as Emma
Emma has 7 times as many as Isaac
items.e: Isaac's bar is 7 equal parts, and each part is the same as Emma's bar (4). So Isaac has 7 times as many: 7 × 4 = 28.

items.q: 40 = 8 × 5 means 40 is 8 times as many as 5. What else does it mean?
items.e: 40 = 8 × 5 can be read two ways: 40 is 8 times as many as 5, and 40 is 5 times as many as 8. “More than” would mean adding, not multiplying.

items.q: Which equation shows “72 is 9 times as many as 8”?
items.e: “9 times as many as 8” means 9 groups of 8, so multiply: 9 × 8 = 72. The equation is 72 = 9 × 8.

items.q: What number makes the sentence true? ☐ is 6 times as many as 9.
items.e: 6 times as many as 9 is 6 × 9 = 54. Adding (9 + 6 = 15) would give “6 more than 9”.

items.q: What does the bar model show?
c: Camila has 18 times as many as Ximena
Ximena has 6 times as many as Camila
Camila has 6 times as many as Ximena
items.e: Camila's bar is 6 equal parts, and each part is the same as Ximena's bar (3). So Camila has 6 times as many: 6 × 3 = 18.

items.q: 42 = 7 × 6 means 42 is 7 times as many as 6. What else does it mean?
items.e: 42 = 7 × 6 can be read two ways: 42 is 7 times as many as 6, and 42 is 6 times as many as 7. “More than” would mean adding, not multiplying.

items.q: A cat weighs 9 pounds. A dog weighs 7 times as much as the cat. The dog weighs 63 pounds. Which equation compares their weights?
items.e: The dog weighs 7 times as much as the cat: 7 × 9 = 63. So 63 = 7 × 9.

items.q: Noah is 9 years old. His aunt is 4 times as old as Noah. His aunt is 36. Which equation compares their ages?
items.e: The aunt's age is 4 times Noah's age: 4 × 9 = 36. So 36 = 4 × 9.

items.q: What number makes the sentence true? 15 is ☐ times as many as 5.
items.e: Think: ☐ × 5 = 15. 3 × 5 = 15, so 15 is 3 times as many as 5. 15 − 5 = 10 tells how many more, not how many times.

sets.title: Multi-step problems: equations, remainders and estimates

items.q: Harper has 23 marbles. Isabella has 5 times as many marbles as Harper. Isabella shares all of her marbles equally among 8 friends, giving each friend as many as possible. How many marbles are left over?
items.e: Step 1: Isabella's marbles: 5 × 23 = 115. Step 2: 115 ÷ 8 = 14 R 3. Each friend gets 14. Step 3: The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder. So the answer is 3 marbles.

items.q: A pond has 37 frogs. It has 5 times as many tadpoles as frogs. How many frogs and tadpoles are in the pond in all? Which equation can you use to find p?
items.e: Step 1: Tadpoles: 5 × 37 = 185. Step 2: In all: 37 + 185 = 222. Put the steps together: 37 + 5 × 37 = p, so p = 222 animals.

items.q: A bakery made 37 muffins in the morning. In the afternoon, it made 3 times as many. It packs the afternoon muffins in boxes of 6. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Step 1: Afternoon muffins: 3 × 37 = 111. Step 2: 111 ÷ 6 = 18 R 3. Step 3: The 3 muffins left over are not enough to fill another box, so leave them out. So the answer is 18 boxes.

items.q: A mother dog weighs 56 pounds. That is 7 times as much as her puppy weighs. How much do the mother and the puppy weigh together?
items.e: Step 1: The puppy: 56 ÷ 7 = 8 pounds. Step 2: Together: 56 + 8 = 64. So the answer is 64 pounds.

items.q: A small concert hall has 395 seats. A stadium has 5 times as many seats. About how many seats does the stadium have? Round to the nearest hundred first.
items.e: 395 rounds to 400. 5 × 400 = 2,000. The exact answer, 395 × 5 = 1,975, is close to 2,000.

items.q: A school trip has 6 adults. There are 7 times as many students as adults. Each van holds 9 people. How many vans are needed for all the students and adults?
items.e: Step 1: Students: 7 × 6 = 42. Step 2: Everyone: 6 + 42 = 48 people. Step 3: 48 ÷ 9 = 5 R 3. The other 3 people still need a van, so add 1. So the answer is 6 vans.

items.q: The third grade collected 61 cans of food. The fourth grade collected 4 times as many cans. The fourth grade packs its cans in boxes of 8. How many boxes does it need for all its cans?
items.e: Step 1: Fourth grade cans: 4 × 61 = 244. Step 2: 244 ÷ 8 = 30 R 4. Step 3: 30 boxes hold 240 cans. The other 4 cans still need a box, so add 1. So the answer is 31 boxes.

items.q: A sandwich costs $10. A party platter costs 6 times as much as the sandwich. Isaac pays for the platter with a $100 bill. How much change does he get? Which equation can you use to find c?
items.e: Step 1: The platter: 6 × $10 = $60. Step 2: Change: $100 − $60 = $40. Put the steps together: 100 − 6 × 10 = c, so c = $40.

items.q: A school garden grew 36 carrots. It grew 6 times as many radishes as carrots. The students picked 178 radishes. How many radishes are still in the garden? Which equation can you use to find r?
items.e: Step 1: Radishes: 6 × 36 = 216. Step 2: Still in the garden: 216 − 178 = 38. Put the steps together: 6 × 36 − 178 = r, so r = 38 radishes.

items.q: A T-shirt costs $12. A jacket costs 5 times as much as the T-shirt. Carlos pays for the jacket with a $100 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Step 1: The jacket: 5 × $12 = $60. Step 2: Change: $100 − $60 = $40. So the answer is $40.

items.q: Mia saved $15. Lucia saved 3 times as much money as Mia. Together they buy a gift that costs $48. How much money do they have left?
items.e: Step 1: Lucia saved 3 × $15 = $45. Step 2: Together: $15 + $45 = $60. Step 3: Left: $60 − $48 = $12. So the answer is $12.

items.q: One class made 19 paper cranes. Another class made 6 times as many. The second class hangs its cranes equally on 3 strings. How many cranes are on each string? Which equation can you use to find c?
items.e: Step 1: The second class: 6 × 19 = 114. Step 2: Each string: 114 ÷ 3 = 38. Put the steps together: 6 × 19 ÷ 3 = c, so c = 38 cranes.

items.q: A school has 1,141 students. The whole town has 6 times as many children. Gabriel says the town has 6,846 children. Use rounding to check. Is his answer reasonable?
c: No, it should be close to 1,000
No, it should be close to 6,000
items.e: 1,141 rounds to 1,000. Estimate: 6 × 1,000 = 6,000. His answer, 6,846, is close to 6,000, so it is reasonable.

items.q: A farm stand sold 378 pounds of apples in September. In October, it sold 4 times as many pounds. About how many pounds did it sell in October? Round to the nearest hundred first.
items.e: 378 rounds to 400. 4 × 400 = 1,600. The exact answer, 378 × 4 = 1,512, is close to 1,600.

items.q: A pickup truck can carry 1,750 pounds. A dump truck can carry 4 times as much. Camila says the dump truck can carry 4,800 pounds. Use rounding to check. Is her answer reasonable?
c: No, it should be close to 2,000
No, it should be close to 8,000
items.e: 1,750 rounds to 2,000. Estimate: 4 × 2,000 = 8,000. Her answer, 4,800, is far from 8,000, so it is not reasonable. Camila forgot to regroup. The exact answer is 1,750 × 4 = 7,000.

items.q: A school library has 385 picture books. The town library has 6 times as many picture books. About how many picture books does the town library have? Round to the nearest hundred first.
items.e: 385 rounds to 400. 6 × 400 = 2,400. The exact answer, 385 × 6 = 2,310, is close to 2,400.

items.q: The third grade read 69 books this month. The fourth grade read 4 times as many books as the third grade. How many books did the two grades read in all?
items.e: Step 1: Fourth grade: 4 × 69 = 276. Step 2: In all: 69 + 276 = 345. So the answer is 345 books.

items.q: Aaliyah has 14 trading cards. Sofia has 4 times as many cards as Aaliyah. Then Sofia gives 37 cards to her cousin. How many cards does Sofia have now?
items.e: Step 1: Sofia's cards: 4 × 14 = 56. Step 2: After giving: 56 − 37 = 19. So the answer is 19 cards.

items.q: An office building is 116 feet tall. That is 4 times as tall as a house. How much taller is the office building than the house? Which equation can you use to find t?
items.e: Step 1: The house: 116 ÷ 4 = 29 feet. Step 2: How much taller: 116 − 29 = 87. Put the steps together: 116 − 116 ÷ 4 = t, so t = 87 feet.

items.q: A small fish tank has 5 fish. A medium tank has 4 times as many fish as the small tank. A big tank has 5 times as many fish as the medium tank. How many fish are in the big tank?
items.e: Step 1: Medium tank: 4 × 5 = 20. Step 2: Big tank: 5 × 20 = 100. So the answer is 100 fish.

items.q: A dump truck can carry 10,800 pounds, and a pickup truck can carry 1,800 pounds. How many times as much as the pickup can the dump truck carry?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 1,800 = 10,800. 6 × 1,800 = 10,800, so the answer is 6. 10,800 − 1,800 = 9,000 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: A bakery sold 1,112 cookies on Saturday. That is 8 times as many cookies as muffins. How many muffins did it sell?
items.e: The bigger amount, 1,112, is 8 equal parts. Each part is the smaller amount, so divide: 1,112 ÷ 8 = 139. Check: 8 × 139 = 1,112. Answer: 139 muffins.

items.q: Caleb rode his bike 80 miles this month, and Aaliyah rode 20 miles. How many times as far as Aaliyah did Caleb ride?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 20 = 80. 4 × 20 = 80, so the answer is 4. 80 − 20 = 60 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: An oak tree is 35 feet tall. It is 7 times as tall as a rose bush. How tall is the rose bush?

items.q: An office building is 272 feet tall. It is 8 times as tall as a house. How tall is the house?

items.q: A concert hall has 1,500 seats, and a small theater has 300 seats. How many times as many seats as the theater does the hall have?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 300 = 1,500. 5 × 300 = 1,500, so the answer is 5. 1,500 − 300 = 1,200 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: A blue whale is 90 feet long, and a dolphin is 10 feet long. How many times as long as the dolphin is the whale?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 10 = 90. 9 × 10 = 90, so the answer is 9. 90 − 10 = 80 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: Isaac saved $100, and Nevaeh saved $20. How many times as much money as Nevaeh did Isaac save?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 20 = 100. 5 × 20 = 100, so the answer is 5. 100 − 20 = 80 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: Isaac has 135 stickers. Nevaeh has 15 stickers. How many times as many stickers as Nevaeh does Isaac have?

items.q: Camila read 600 pages this week. That is 8 times as many pages as Mateo read. How many pages did Mateo read?

items.q: A laptop costs $1,060. That is 5 times as much as a tablet costs. How much does the tablet cost?
items.e: The bigger amount, $1,060, is 5 equal parts. Each part is the smaller amount, so divide: $1,060 ÷ 5 = $212. Check: 5 × $212 = $1,060. Answer: $212.

items.q: A library has 6,024 books. That is 8 times as many books as DVDs. How many DVDs does the library have?
items.e: The bigger amount, 6,024, is 8 equal parts. Each part is the smaller amount, so divide: 6,024 ÷ 8 = 753. Check: 8 × 753 = 6,024. Answer: 753 DVDs.

items.q: A city has 6,225 people. That is 3 times as many people as a nearby town has. How many people live in the town?
items.e: The bigger amount, 6,225, is 3 equal parts. Each part is the smaller amount, so divide: 6,225 ÷ 3 = 2,075. Check: 3 × 2,075 = 6,225. Answer: 2,075 people.

items.q: A bike costs $140. A board game costs $20. How many times as much as the game does the bike cost?

items.q: A mother dog weighs 32 pounds. That is 4 times as much as her puppy weighs. How much does the puppy weigh?

items.q: The big tank at a pet store has 68 fish. That is 4 times as many fish as the small tank has. How many fish are in the small tank?

items.q: A blue ribbon is 60 inches long, and a red ribbon is 20 inches long. How many times as long as the red ribbon is the blue ribbon?
items.e: To find “how many times”, divide the bigger amount by the smaller one. Think: ☐ × 20 = 60. 3 × 20 = 60, so the answer is 3. 60 − 20 = 40 tells how many more, not how many times.

items.q: A farm has 252 chickens. That is 7 times as many chickens as cows. How many cows does the farm have?

items.q: A bathtub holds 48 gallons of water, and a bucket holds 6 gallons. How many times as much water as the bucket does the bathtub hold?

items.q: An orchard has 325 apple trees and 65 pear trees. How many times as many apple trees as pear trees does it have?
